one_line_contribution: A measurement paper that defines a substitution ratio S — the fraction of an ExpeL-style bank's paired memory gain that disappears once a reflective prompt optimizer (GEPA) is given exactly the same training episodes — and adds a frozen 'compile the whole bank into one static instruction and delete retrieval' arm (C/M2) plus a deliberately non-compilable near-duplicate bank (B-dup) so that a null on S is interpretable rather than a power failure.
closest_prior_work: ExpeL itself (2308.10144), which the proposal treats only as a target. ExpeL's pipeline already separates two containers — extracted insights, which are appended statically to the instruction, and retrieved successful trajectories used as demonstrations — and its own ablations report both contributing. Arm C ('a frontier model reads the entire bank offline and compiles it into one static instruction block, no retrieval at inference') is close to ExpeL-insights-only, and ExpeL's published ablation is direct evidence against Falsifiable Prediction 3. The Related Work section never mentions this ablation, which is the single most damaging omission in the novelty argument. Two further real precedents are unaddressed: (a) MIPROv2/DSPy already optimizes instructions and bootstrapped demonstrations as separable slots and reports instruction-only vs demo-only vs joint ablations — that is a published controlled comparison of exactly the two containers the proposal claims the field has never compared; (b) Agent Workflow Memory (Wang et al., 2024) induces reusable workflows from training episodes in an offline setting and injects them as static prompt text, which is arm C for web agents. None of these individually make S novel, but together they mean the 'compile, don't retrieve' prediction is a re-test of existing ablations rather than a new hypothesis, and only the matched-information constraint and the ratio endpoint remain genuinely new.
strongest_objection: The design cannot confirm its own headline predictions, by the authors' own stated rules. Measurement gives a per-cell-pair MDE of ~4 points at n=600 and ~5.6 points for a change in the memory gain, and Limitation 6 commits to reporting sub-MDE differences as 'inconclusive in either direction.' But Prediction 3 — which the proposal itself calls 'the risky, non-obvious prediction' — asserts that I0xM2 comes 'within 2 points' of I0xM1; Prediction 7 asserts I0xM1 exceeds I0xM3 by '<3 points'; Prediction 2 asserts I3 recovers '<20% of I1's improvement' (about 1 point if I1-I0 is ~5). All three are equivalence claims strictly inside the MDE, and no equivalence procedure (TOST, a declared margin, a power calculation for equivalence) appears anywhere in Measurement and Noise Control — only NHST with McNemar and Holm. A non-significant I0xM2 vs I0xM1 difference will therefore be reported as 'compilation matches retrieval' when it is simply absence of evidence, and applying Limitation 6 honestly means Predictions 2, 3 and 7 can be refuted but never confirmed. Only Predictions 1, 4 and 6 are resolvable at this power. Compounding this, the primary endpoint's denominator is not measured but manufactured: the PRECHECK GATE says a bank that fails the 10-point dev gate 'is enriched (more training episodes, better distillation) until it passes.' That does two bad things. It selects the denominator on a 150-instance dev split for being large, so the test-split denominator regresses downward and the whole MDE argument ('the predicted drop of ≥6 points sits above the MDE') may not hold when S is actually computed; and adding training episodes to the bank breaks the equal-training-episode constraint that Experiments calls 'the fairness constraint that makes the study interpretable,' since GEPA is not re-run on the enriched split. A reviewer will also note the internal tension with the track's own starting position: at k=7 a full retrieved bank was measured to fix zero items and break six to seven, yet this plan fixes top-k=7 and requires a +10-point gain from it before any cell is run.
what_would_fix_it: 1) Pre-register the bank: freeze construction before any dev measurement, forbid the enrichment loop, and if the gate must exist, gate on a split disjoint from both optimization and test and report the shrinkage. Better, replace the gate with a rule that S is reported only when the test-split denominator's lower CI bound exceeds 8 points, and otherwise report the two paired differences separately instead of their ratio. 2) Re-specify Predictions 2, 3 and 7 as equivalence tests with a declared margin and a power calculation for that margin; at a 2-point margin on paired binary outcomes this likely needs n well above 600 or a matched-pairs design with more decoding seeds, and it is better to know that now than to publish a sub-MDE tie as a match. 3) Restore I2 and add a k sweep (see missing_baseline). 4) Add a no-episode instruction-rewrite control so the matched-information premise is actually tested. 5) Drop Prediction 5 or power it — a top-decile subgroup is n=60 against a ~4-point MDE, so 'the bottom 70% shows a residual gain whose CI covers zero' is guaranteed regardless of truth. 6) Verify every 2026 citation by hand and report which were confirmed, given the retraction of five in the previous draft. 7) Fix the incoherent 'token-matched per instance' spec for the static arm C: a frozen block cannot vary per instance without becoming a retrieval system, so state whether the match is on the mean and what is truncated.
missing_baseline: A no-episode instruction-rewrite control: an instruction produced by the same frontier model from the task description and the hand-written I0 alone, with zero access to any training episode, token-matched to I1. Without it, a high S is equally explained by 'a frontier model wrote a better scaffold for a 14B agent' as by the paper's thesis that instruction and memory are two containers for the same episode-derived information; I3 padded with 'task-generic boilerplate' controls length, not content provenance, so the causal claim about matched information is untested. Two further omissions a reviewer will demand: (a) a retrieval-budget arm (k=3 alongside k=7) — the track's own measured result is that injection volume, not memory content, was the causal lever, so fixing k=7 makes both the S denominator and the I0xM2-vs-I0xM1 verdict functions of an untuned hyperparameter, and a compiled-static win over k=7 that vanishes against k=3 refutes the practical recommendation; (b) I2, GEPA optimized with memory in context, which is cut as 'co-adaptation, not substitution' but is the only realistic deployment pairing — measuring memory's residual on top of an instruction that was optimized to work without memory biases the numerator of S downward and S upward, and it is question 4 of the track brief.
preprint_collision: The check has the right shape — it names a closest work, separates genus from claim, states residual risk, and openly retracts prior citations — and that self-correction is more than most submissions do. But it does not establish novelty. Every load-bearing 2026 reference (MemDelta 2606.29914, EvoClinician 2601.22964, 2603.02473, 2605.21768, 2603.18272) is unverifiable to me, and the check itself reports that the previous draft cited five papers (ActMem 2603.00026, MAS-PromptBench 2606.23664, TERMS-Bench 2605.13909, MemAPO 2603.21520, 2602.11243) that the current search could not return and that all reliance on them was removed. A search tool demonstrated within this same document to emit references that cannot be re-found cannot then be trusted to certify that the closest work is MemDelta; the correct remedy is per-citation manual verification with a stated confirmation status, which is absent. The check also concedes it never swept OpenReview 2026 — the single most likely home for a 'GEPA vs memory bank' ablation, given GEPA is itself an ICLR 2026 oral — and the flagged TERMS-Bench, described as a GEPA-based substitution test for a non-prompt intervention, would be a direct precedent for the logical move if it exists. Most importantly, the check searches only for collisions on framing and misses the collisions that actually bite, which are ablations inside the papers being targeted: ExpeL's insights-only versus retrieved-demonstrations ablation, MIPROv2's instruction-versus-demonstration ablations in DSPy, and offline workflow induction in Agent Workflow Memory. Net: a thin check on the axis that matters, and I treat the novelty claim as unestablished rather than merely unverified.
